sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's bind operator silently propagates Nothing through an entire chain of computations, so once absence appears, every subsequent step yields Nothing without ever being evaluated.
sketches.resonance: Once someone is gone, every future you imagined with them collapses into nothing, one after another, without anyone needing to say why.
sketches.draft:
future :: Maybe a -> Maybe b -> Maybe c -> Maybe c
future you me us =
  you >> me >> us

-- future (Just _) Nothing _ == Nothing

sketches.mechanism: A static local variable persists across function calls — it survives the function's death and rebirth, carrying its value forward invisibly, never accessible from outside.
sketches.resonance: Some things you carry are invisible to everyone else, but every time you return to the same place, they're still there, changed by the last visit.

sketches.mechanism: The 'never' return type indicates a function that cannot possibly return — the type system guarantees the caller will never receive a value back.
sketches.resonance: Some departures are encoded in the structure of things: not that you chose not to come back, but that coming back was never a possible type.
